topic: Heading to the snow in Japan? Prepare your knees

slides.headline: Japan ski trip booked? Train your knees
slides.sub: A few weeks of prep can make day three feel a lot better.

slides.title: Why knees often feel it first
slides.body: Skiing and snowboarding keep you in a bent-knee position for long runs, with twisting and sudden loads. After a Sydney summer, most legs aren't used to that, so thighs tire and knees work harder.

slides.title: Start four to six weeks out
slides.body: Two or three leg sessions a week is a good starting point: squats, split squats, step-downs and wall sits. Build up gradually so you arrive strong rather than sore from cramming.

slides.title: Train balance and side-to-side
slides.body: Single-leg balance, side lunges and small lateral hops help your knees cope with uneven snow and quick corrections. Start slowly and keep each knee travelling in line with your toes.

slides.title: Pace the first few days
slides.body: Jet lag, cold and long lift lines add up. Keep day one shorter, take regular breaks and finish before your legs are cooked. Tired legs often mean sloppier technique late in the day.

slides.title: When to get it checked
slides.body: A pop with swelling within a few hours, a knee that gives way or locks, or being unable to take weight are worth an assessment, on the mountain or once you're home.

slides.headline: Want a pre-trip knee check?
slides.body: Our Sydney CBD and Chatswood physios can check your leg strength and balance, then set a simple plan to follow before you fly. Book online — link in bio.

caption:
Japan ski trip booked? Your knees would like a few weeks' notice. ⛷️

Skiing and snowboarding hold you in a bent-knee position for long runs, with plenty of twisting and sudden loads. After months of beach days, most legs aren't quite ready for that.

A good starting point is two or three leg sessions a week for four to six weeks: squats, split squats, step-downs, wall sits and some single-leg balance work. Once you're there, keep the first day shorter and stop before your legs are cooked.

A pop with swelling, a knee that gives way or locks, or not being able to take weight is worth getting assessed.
